parsedVerdict.reasoning: LendingService sits in the business (domain) layer, and its responsibilities fit that role. It enforces lending rules: loan length must be 1–60 days, a member must be able to borrow, and a book must have a copy to check out or check in. It also sets the fine policy (FINE_PER_DAY, daysLate * FINE_PER_DAY) and runs the lend and return use cases using the Book, Loan and Member domain objects. Storage is handled by the injected gateways (findById, openLoansOf, updateCopies, insert, markReturned). The service has no SQL, connection handling, query building, HTTP or request/response handling, serialisation or framework code. Building domain objects from the plain records the gateways return is the usual Table Data Gateway arrangement for a domain or service layer. It is not persistence logic. The in-memory loan ID counter (`loan-${this.sequence}`) is a weak design choice: IDs are not unique across restarts or instances. But it does not clearly belong to another layer kind. Whether the business layer may depend on the persistence gateways at all is an import-direction question, which is out of scope here.
